identity.operation: Dump a JSON value through do_dump.
identity.capability: do_dump returns failure at the depth limit.

requirement: For a reachable value at the depth limit, dumping must return failure.

assessment.necessity_reason: The dump API supports a finite constructed JSON value deeper than JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH, and do_dump now fails when traversal reaches that depth. The old harness dumps only values returned by json_loadb. Parsing rejects values beyond the limit; with parsing starting at depth 1 and dumping at depth 0, a successfully parsed value cannot reach the dump guard. Neither dump mode constructs a deeper value.

before.requirement: Reach a clean do_dump failure when traversal reaches JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH.
before.reason: The complete old do_dump body has no depth limit rejection.

after.requirement: Reach the supported do_dump failure for a JSON value whose traversal reaches JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH.
after.reason: The new guard returns failure at the limit. The API test supplies an array beyond the limit, but the harness sends only successfully parsed values to dumping. parse_value rejects values beyond the limit, while dump traversal begins one depth level lower than parsing. The harness has no other route to a deeper value.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Array dumping recursively increases traversal depth.
The API test supplies nested arrays beyond the limit and checks that dumping fails.
json_loadb returns the value produced by parse_json.
Parsing starts at depth zero and delegates value construction to parse_value.
parse_value increments depth and rejects values beyond JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH.
Callback dumping invokes do_dump at depth zero; string dumping delegates to callback dumping.

assessment.comparison_reason: The same depth limit tuple is absent from old do_dump and supported by new do_dump. The old harness cannot reach the new behavior because its only dumped objects come from the depth limited parser.

necessity_evidence.reason: The after source supports a dump failure at the depth limit for constructed nested arrays. The fixed harness dumps only values accepted by json_loadb. Parsing starts at depth zero, counts the root as depth one, and rejects values beyond the limit; dumping starts at depth zero. Its parsed values therefore cannot reach the new guard. The before do_dump had no such guard, so this coverage obligation was introduced.
necessity_evidence.finite_witness: Let N be the configured JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH. Construct a JSON array nested N+100 levels, then call json_dumps on it with flags 0; the supplied API test expects failure. No fuzzer input can supply that value to this target's dump calls: every dumped value must first pass json_loadb, which rejects the required nesting.

scope_contract.reason: Dumping JSON values is a primary target operation. The after dump contract includes failure at traversal depth N, and the API test demonstrates that constructed nested arrays are supported dump inputs. The contract is observable through json_dumps and json_dump_callback.

evidence.dependency_reason: The API test demonstrates a constructed nested array as a supported dump input and checks depth-limit failure.
json_dumps exposes callback-dump failure as a null result.

feasible_trigger.reason: The after API test specifies a finite constructed array deeper than N and checks its dump failure. Array traversal increments dump depth, so that setup reaches the guard. The target cannot create that setup from its input because it dumps only successfully parsed values.

evidence.dependency_reason: Specifies the finite constructed-array setup and expected failure.
Parsing rejects a value whose parse depth exceeds N.

observable_consequence.reason: At traversal depth N, do_dump returns failure. json_dump_callback returns that result, while json_dumps converts it to NULL. This specific supported failure is unreachable in the fixed target.

evidence.dependency_reason: Callback dumping propagates the do_dump result.
String dumping converts callback-dump failure to NULL.
The API test checks the externally visible null result.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: Both target dump modes do reach do_dump, but only with the value returned by json_loadb. parse_json begins at depth zero, parse_value counts the root as depth one and rejects depth above N, and do_dump begins at depth zero. Thus even a maximally deep parsed value reaches only dump depth N−1. The complete target entry has no construction or mutation route to a deeper value.

evidence.dependency_reason: json_loadb returns the parse_json result that the target passes to dumping.
parse_json initializes parse depth to zero and calls parse_value.
parse_value increments depth for each value and rejects depth above N.
Callback dumping invokes do_dump at depth zero.
The other dump mode delegates to callback dumping.

identity_preserved.reason: The same tuple is assessed on both versions: dump traversal at depth N and failure there. The complete before do_dump lacks the guard; the after do_dump has it. The same fixed harness supplies parsed values to dumping on both sides.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Shows the supported finite constructed-array case and expected dump failure.
Bounds the depth of values accepted by the parser.
Sets initial parse depth and delegates to parse_value.
Starts dump traversal at depth zero and propagates its result.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: Dumping a constructed JSON array whose traversal reaches JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH fails cleanly.
coverage_witness.required_setup: Construct an array nested deeper than JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH and pass it to json_dumps or json_dump_callback.
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: The fixed entry passes only successfully json_loadb-parsed values to its dump calls.
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: Neither dump call can reach do_dump at the depth-limit guard.
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: The string and callback modes both dump the same parser-bounded value; neither constructs or deepens it.
